analysis: All changes are in the advisory threat-review CI tooling (.github/scripts/threat_review/*), a changelog fragment and docs/developer/build.md. None touch the provider, coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011), keys or attestation assets, so the provider threat entries (T-052..T-058 etc.) are not affected. Observations: (1) state.py WRITE_ATTEMPTS 8->12 and a longer jittered backoff (0.5-8s) apply only to explicit 409 conflicts. Ledger mutate() still re-reads and re-checks caps on each attempt, and exhaustion still raises BudgetStopped, so fail-closed spend control is preserved. Paid calls are not repeated. The new error.diagnostic.update(...) in save_cache/checkpoint (state.py:185, 206) runs after write() has set error.diagnostic (lines 72-73), so the attribute always exists; it adds only integers. (2) integration_context.py:20-22 renames replayed unit id to source_id so replayed units cannot be confused with primary acknowledgment targets. This narrows, not widens, the acknowledgment scope; replayed text is still untrusted evidence. (3) diagnostics.py:82 adds a response_repairs snapshot field to the diagnostics artifact that is uploaded to Actions. The producer of response_repairs is not in the supplied evidence, so I cannot confirm it holds only content-free metadata (codes, counts, hashes) rather than model-response or source text. The next pass should check that producer. The changelog also claims rejection of final results from another workflow run/attempt and retention of findings on usage-accounting failure; the code implementing this is not in this batch (likely client/runner/report modules) and was not verified. No concrete regression was identified from the visible lines.
